subject: Oceanography
title: Predicting ENSO
description: A quick, practical guide to Predicting ENSO.

hook.text: A line of buoys stretches across the tropical Pacific—sensing the ocean's mood before El Niño strikes.

buildup.text: The TAO/TRITON array monitors temperature, winds, and currents in real time across the equatorial Pacific.

discovery.text: Coupled ocean-atmosphere models can now predict ENSO events 6–9 months in advance.

twist.text: Despite progress, the 'spring predictability barrier' makes forecasts issued in March unreliable for later that year.

climax.text: Better ENSO forecasts save billions—farmers adjust crops, water managers prepare, and disaster agencies mobilize.

punchline.text: Predicting the Pacific's mood months ahead saves lives and livelihoods.

quiz.question: How far ahead can ENSO be predicted?
